gaps.title: Delegate parallel execution with result aggregation
gaps.exists: SubPlanDispatcher exists in workflow/delegate/sub-plan.ts with parallel/sequential/mixed execution. DelegateBroker has full lifecycle. But no result aggregation service — SubPlanResult is a plain type, no MapReduce-style aggregation, no timeout/cancellation coordination across parallel sub-plans.
gaps.missing: ParallelResultAggregator that collects results from parallel sub-plans with timeout handling, partial result collection, and configurable aggregation strategy (merge-all, first-N, majority-vote). Integration with SubPlanDispatcher for coordinated parallel execution.
deps: C9 (EventBus replay for recovering lost sub-plan results)
gaps.risk: LOW — extending SubPlanDispatcher, no breaking changes

gaps.title: LLM cross-provider automatic fallback chain
gaps.exists: CircuitBreaker + CircuitBreakerRegistry exist in services/circuit-breaker.ts. LLMServiceImpl has provider Map + fallback in getProvider() that skips open-circuit providers. ProviderFallbackChain exists in gateway/provider-fallback.ts but is gateway-scoped.
gaps.missing: LLMFallbackChain service that provides automatic fallback across providers: primary → secondary → tertiary with configurable retry policy per provider. Latency-based provider selection. Fallback event publishing via IEventBus. Integration with CircuitBreakerRegistry for health-aware selection.
gaps.risk: MEDIUM — modifying LLM service call paths; must preserve existing behavior

gaps.title: Quality gate feedback loop (verify → plan gap → re-execute)
gaps.exists: ArtifactContract + ArtifactResolver exist in workflow/artifact-contract.ts. Workflow stages (analyze/plan/execute/verify) exist in state.json. No feedback loop mechanism — verification gaps don't automatically feed back into planning.
gaps.missing: QualityGateFeedbackLoop that: reads verification.json gaps, maps them to plan tasks, generates re-execution sub-plans, tracks fix iterations, and escalates after max retries. Event-driven: publishes gap-detected events, subscribes to fix-completed events.
gaps.risk: HIGH — new workflow orchestration layer; must not interfere with existing stage progression

gaps.title: Obsidian ↔ Knowledge bidirectional real-time sync
gaps.exists: NowledgeGraphSync exists with bidirectional Knowledge↔Graph sync. IObsidianService has read/write/search. IKnowledgeService has CRUD. No real-time sync between Obsidian vault and Knowledge store — sync is request-driven, not event-driven.
gaps.missing: ObsidianKnowledgeSync that: watches Obsidian vault changes (file create/modify/delete), syncs to Knowledge store in real-time; listens to Knowledge store change events, syncs back to Obsidian. Conflict resolution strategy. Debounced batch sync for performance. EventBus integration for change notifications.
gaps.risk: MEDIUM — Obsidian file system interaction; must handle concurrent writes gracefully

gaps.title: Graph ↔ Wiki link resolution bridge
gaps.exists: GraphEngineAdapter in DI. IObsidianService has vault operations. NowledgeGraphSync has entity/relation sync. No link resolution — graph edges don't resolve to wiki pages and vice versa.
gaps.missing: GraphWikiLinkBridge that: resolves graph entity IDs to wiki page paths, resolves wiki [[links]] to graph nodes, maintains bidirectional link index, handles orphaned/dangling links. Integration with IGraphEngine for traversal and IObsidianService for page resolution.
deps: C4 (real-time sync keeps link index fresh)
gaps.risk: LOW — additive bridge service, no existing code changes

gaps.title: MCP Gateway service discovery + health monitoring
gaps.exists: MCPRequestRouter exists with capability-based routing. ProviderFallbackChain exists. No service discovery — providers are statically registered. No health monitoring — circuit breaker tracks failures but no proactive health checks.
gaps.missing: MCPServiceDiscovery that: discovers providers dynamically (file-based, config-based, or registry-based), registers them with MCPRequestRouter. MCPHealthMonitor that: performs periodic health checks (ping/health endpoint), updates provider health status in MCPRequestRouter, publishes health events via IEventBus, triggers circuit breaker state transitions on health changes.
gaps.risk: MEDIUM — gateway is external-facing; service discovery must be secure

gaps.title: Workflow engine parallel wave execution
gaps.exists: SubPlanDispatcher supports parallel/sequential/mixed execution. Plan.json defines waves with parallel tasks. No wave execution engine — plan waves are not automatically executed by the workflow engine.
gaps.missing: WaveExecutionEngine that: reads plan.json waves, executes tasks within each wave in parallel, waits for wave completion before advancing, handles wave-level failure (retry/skip/abort), publishes wave lifecycle events via IEventBus. Integration with existing workflow engine for stage progression.
gaps.risk: HIGH — core workflow orchestration; must preserve sequential stage guarantees

gaps.title: Search result relevance scoring + cache invalidation
gaps.exists: UnifiedSearchPipeline with RRF fusion scoring. HybridSearch has scoring. SearchStrategyConfig has profiles. No explicit relevance scoring beyond RRF — no learning/ranking model. No cache invalidation — search results are not cached.
gaps.missing: SearchRelevanceScorer that: applies configurable relevance scoring beyond RRF (recency boost, source authority, query expansion), tracks click-through / selection signals for learning. SearchCacheManager that: caches search results with TTL, invalidates on knowledge/Obsidian changes via IEventBus, supports cache warming for common queries.
gaps.risk: LOW — extending search pipeline with optional components, no breaking changes

gaps.title: Event bus replay + dead-letter queue
gaps.exists: TypedEventBus in services/event-bus.ts with publish/subscribe/wildcard. No event persistence — events are in-process only, lost on crash. No replay mechanism. No dead-letter handling — failed handler calls throw and are lost.
gaps.missing: EventBusReplay that: persists events to configurable store (in-memory ring buffer by default, pluggable for persistent), replays events from a given timestamp/sequence, supports snapshot-based replay for efficiency. DeadLetterQueue that: captures events that failed handler processing, provides retry mechanism with backoff, exposes dead-letter inspection and manual replay. Integration with existing TypedEventBus.
gaps.risk: MEDIUM — extending EventBus; must not impact synchronous dispatch performance

gaps.title: Full-stack integration test suite
gaps.exists: Individual unit tests exist for Phase 1/2 features. No integration tests that exercise cross-service workflows (e.g., LLM fallback → circuit breaker → event bus notification → search cache invalidation).
gaps.missing: Integration test suite covering: (1) LLM fallback chain with circuit breaker, (2) Search pipeline with strategy config and cache, (3) Workflow execution with artifact contracts, (4) EventBus pub/sub with replay and dead-letter, (5) MCP Gateway routing with health monitoring, (6) Knowledge/Obsidian bidirectional sync, (7) Delegate parallel execution with result aggregation, (8) Wave execution engine end-to-end. Target: >= 80% integration coverage.
gaps.risk: LOW — test-only, no production code changes

execution_order.reason: Foundational: C2 LLM fallback chain extends Phase 2 circuit breaker independently; C9 EventBus replay+DLQ is a keystone — C1/C3/C4/C6/C7/C8 all depend on it
Dependent on C9 (EventBus): C1 parallel aggregation, C4 Obsidian↔Knowledge sync, C6 MCP discovery+health, C8 search scoring+cache. C2 is done so LLM fallback is available.
Higher-order: C3 quality gate feedback loop (needs C1+C9), C5 Graph↔Wiki bridge (needs C4), C7 wave execution engine (needs C1+C9)
Integration test suite runs after all C1-C9 are implemented

key_insights: C9 (EventBus replay + dead-letter queue) is the keystone — 6 of 9 other gaps depend on it
C2 (LLM fallback chain) is independent and can start immediately with Phase 2 circuit breaker
C3 (Quality gate feedback loop) is the most complex — requires C1 and C9, introduces new workflow orchestration
C7 (Wave execution engine) is the second most complex — requires C1 and C9, touches core workflow
C10 (Integration tests) must come last but is LOW complexity — purely test code
Risk profile: 2 LOW, 6 MEDIUM, 2 HIGH — C3 and C7 are the high-risk items
4 waves needed vs Phase 2's 2 waves — reflects deeper dependency graph
